parallel.requirements: Recognized the ESM-only, local-import, manual-argv, /output/test10.mjs, schedule formatting, and executable-probing requirements.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent kept implementation ownership while spawning children for CLI/output probing; /root/probe_cli also proceeded into implementation in the shared /output tree.
parallel.implementation: Parent built argparse, runtime output, schedule job/scheduler/validation modules and an entrypoint, then child /root/probe_cli wrote a competing parser/text/runtime layout and entrypoint.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Parent detected extra child helper files, deleted them, discovered the entrypoint had been overwritten to import them, and reconciled test10.mjs plus facade exports before delivery.
parallel.verification: Parent ran Node checks for normal execution, help, missing args, unknown args, invalid time cases, and final help/normal checks before the official 150/150 pass.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unresolved defect remained at closure, but during integration the shared deliverable was temporarily broken by the child overwrite.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same ESM, manual CLI, local module, schedule formatting, output parity, and /output/test10.mjs requirements without delegation.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One agent owned probing, implementation, patching, verification, and final delivery in sequence with no child work or shared ownership boundary.
serial.implementation: It created argparse, schedule, runtime error, and entrypoint modules in one apply_patch pass, then made targeted patches for error naming and CLI banner parity.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial tree was integrated as one coherent module set with no competing writer, no entrypoint replacement by another actor, and final artifact listing in status.
serial.verification: It ran side-by-side checks against the executable for normal output, help, missing arguments, and invalid daily time behavior before the official pass.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished or incorrect behavior is evidenced at closure; remaining noted difference was only nondeterministic PyInstaller PID text on error paths.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run identified the required pure ESM module tree, manual argv handling, schedule API emulation, exact output formatting, and /output/test10.mjs deliverable.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run identified the same requirements and treated the executable as the reference for stdout, stderr, parser, and .at() behavior.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-coverage difference remained; both recognized the task obligations and passed. The process difference appears later in shared-state handling.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent spawned probe children while also implementing; /root/probe_cli nested another child and then wrote implementation files itself.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run had one owner for all stages and no child trajectories or delegated workspace ownership.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel decomposition overlapped probing and implementation but blurred ownership of the final /output tree; serial ownership was simpler and avoided that coordination boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Children received the task and produced useful probing results, but the implementation child operated without an effective file-ownership boundary for the required entrypoint.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There was no inter-agent interface; the single agent maintained one internal API shape across parser, scheduler, runtime, and entrypoint modules.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The meaningful interface problem in parallel manifested as a concrete write conflict rather than a missing brief or handoff mismatch; serial had no cross-agent interface surface.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parent first implemented modules with apply_patch and tested them, then child code overwrote the entrypoint and parts of the module facade, forcing a later reconciliation patch.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial created the module set once, adjusted error naming and program name formatting, and kept the implementation internally consistent.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both final implementations solved the task, but parallel had an extra repair path caused by competing writes, while serial patches were ordinary self-corrections.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: One probe child returned useful output, the parent waited on running children, listed agents, interrupted /root/probe_cli, and then resolved the visible workspace state itself.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: No child result lifecycle existed; the single agent directly consumed its own command outputs and proceeded to implementation and verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had extra result-management activity, but no retained lifecycle label because the final harmful event was a write overwrite that the parent repaired.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The shared /output tree contained child-written helper files and a child-replaced entrypoint; deleting the helpers caused the entrypoint to fail until the parent reconciled it.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run had no shared-state collision and delivered one coherent /output file set.
comparison_dimensions.difference: This is the material parallel adverse pattern: concurrent shared workspace writes replaced the required deliverable, while serial avoided the collision entirely.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: After reconciling the overwrite, the parent reran normal output, help, missing-argument, unknown-argument, and invalid-time checks before the official pass.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran side-by-side checks, patched the final display differences, and ended with official 150/150 success.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both verified enough to pass; the parallel verification loop additionally caught the overwrite-induced broken entrypoint before closure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used four subagents and more wall time/tokens, but it still repaired the conflict and finished well before the official timeout.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one trajectory, fewer requests, no subagent budget, and completed successfully with a shorter recorded agent duration.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel coordination added overhead and a repair loop but did not exhaust budget or change the pass outcome.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluation is not discordant: parallel and serial both passed 150 of 150 tests. Their final task coverage was materially equivalent, but the parallel path suffered a recoverable shared-state overwrite of the required entrypoint that the serial path avoided.
parallel_contributors: Parallel probing and implementation found the needed CLI and scheduler behavior, then final verification caught and repaired the overwritten entrypoint before closure.
serial_contributors: Serial probing, implementation, and verification were kept in one trajectory, avoiding concurrent file ownership conflicts while still matching the reference behavior.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial made ordinary self-patches for error naming and CLI banner text; those were not concurrency patterns.

candidates.reason: The parent implemented the solution and /root/probe_cli also implemented; the problem was competing ownership, not absence of an implementation owner.
The parent actively inspected, reconciled, patched, and retested the integrated module tree, so integration was not unowned.
The parent owned final assembly of /output/test10.mjs and delivered it; the issue was a temporary overwrite of that deliverable.
The parent controlled the end-to-end flow through implementation, repair, verification, and final answer, with no unowned pipeline transition.
Probing happened in parallel with parent work and did not gate all implementation behind one mandatory serial preflight.
The parent began implementation before all child investigation finished, so investigation was not a completed first phase that delayed implementation.
The indispensable implementation path had active parent capacity and completed; no required critical path was starved by auxiliary work.
Although there were four subagents and high token use, the run did not exhaust the deadline or leave needed work unfinished.
No single delegated scope is shown as overbroad and unfinished in a way that prevented required completion; the observed harm was a write conflict.
The child saw the task and produced/probed relevant behavior; no already-known requirement missing from its brief is the evidenced cause of unusable work.
The agents did have incompatible file/API shapes, but the concrete realized event was a same deliverable replacement, which the write taxonomy handles more specifically.
No known finding is shown disappearing through transfer and causing repeated work; the parent received usable probe information.
Returned probe reports were not too large or unstructured for the parent to use; the adverse event was not unconsumed bulk information.
No receiver acted on a superseded report; the parent responded to the current workspace state after observing the overwrite.
The conflict was not unadjudicated reports at decision time; it was a concrete overwritten entrypoint that the parent repaired.
The parent did not close with a visible unresolved integrated gap; after discovering the broken entrypoint it patched and reran checks.
There was no replacement retry lacking inherited findings; the parent made targeted repairs based on observed current files and test failures.

After the overwrite reconciliation, the parent reran checks, so there was no unverified post-verification merge.
The child implementation was not a clean completed result left unjoined; it had already altered the shared files and was directly reconciled by the parent.
No verifier child produced a concrete finding trapped below the parent; the returned probe information was visible and used.

The parent did wait on children, but then inspected agent state and shared files; no deadline loss from blind waiting is evidenced.
There were overlapping designs across files, but a more specific replacement of the required entrypoint is directly proven.
